goal: Act as DC FEMS dispatch shift supervisor at 09:00 on 2025-01-15: re-triage 15 incoming calls against unit_status.csv, station geography and the CAD database, and assign units. Deliver dispatch_decisions.xlsx (prioritized queue + capability/proximity matrix), conflict_report.csv plus CAD inserts, and shift_handover.xlsx (GIS map data, battalion/specialty depletion, Montgomery County 911 call-pattern analysis, operational notes).
delivered: Four files in output/: dispatch_decisions.xlsx (Prioritized Queue for all 15 calls, Unit Match Matrix), shift_handover.xlsx (4 sheets incl. battalion table, specialty coverage table and Kaggle montcoalert pattern stats on 663,522 records), conflict_report.csv (10 anomaly rows: E11 status conflict, unlinked A15/M5/EMS3, related-incident pairs, end-of-shift, sync count) and dispatch_cad_synced.db with 15 calls / 26 assignments.
what_went_wrong: All six failures are dispatch-judgment or write-up choices made with full information. The agent sent RS1+BC6 (High-angle Rescue per unit_status.csv) to the water rescue instead of recalling E2 or escalating the Swift Water gap, gave the COPD call only BLS A14 while spending M8 on a chest-pain call 5.86 mi away, and made BLS A11 the primary unit on the stroke call without any tPA-window reasoning. The conflict report omitted the ON_SCENE A02 units (E4/T6/BC4/EMS4), the battalion sheet never named E7/M7 as the cause of Battalion 2's reduced coverage, and the call-pattern sheet stripped the 'Traffic:' prefix (rank 1 'VEHICLE ACCIDENT -', 148,372) and labeled the Kaggle data 'context only', so it was not tied to resource positioning.

failed_items.why: Prioritized Queue assigns 'RS1 (water rescue/high-angle squad); BC6' and says E2 is ENROUTE so cannot be double-booked; no recall of E2 and no explicit mutual-aid escalation. The agent's own Unit Match Matrix and Resource Depletion sheet say only E2 has Swift Water Rescue (RS1 is High-angle in unit_status.csv). The geojson does list swift water at the Engine 2 station, so the choice is partly defensible, but it contradicts the agent's own matrix.

conflict_report.csv lists only true anomalies (E11 status mismatch, A15/M5/EMS3 unlinked, related pairs). It never records E4/T6/BC4/EMS4 as ON_SCENE at A02 and unavailable, even though the agent excluded them from dispatch. The agent chose to report only anomalies. The rubric expected all committed units to be listed.

The Resource Depletion sheet gives Battalion 2 as aggregates only (7 units, 2 OOS, flag LOW from post-dispatch depletion of 80%) and never names E7/M7 maintenance as the reason. It also flags ALS 'ZERO AFTER DISPATCH'. The rubric's 8-unit roster is itself wrong: A19 is Battalion 3 in unit_status.csv, so the agent's count of 7 is correct.

Stroke IC-014 is P1 with M4, but A11 (a BLS ambulance at 0.09 mi) is the Primary Unit, and no file mentions tPA or the 3-4.5 h treatment window. The justification only says 'time-sensitive transport is prioritized'.

The agent downloaded the same 663,522-row montcoalert data (step 11-13), but it ranked title suffixes, so the top type appears as 'VEHICLE ACCIDENT -' (148,372, which is 'Traffic: VEHICLE ACCIDENT -'), with a separate 'VEHICLE ACCIDENT' at rank 4. It also states 'Context only; not a D.C. deployment model', so the finding never informs positioning. The judge was wrong that the agent did not use the sample data, but the labeling and framing are the agent's choices.

COPD call IC-010 is P1 but gets only A14 (BLS) as primary ('mutual-aid ALS requested'). All five available medics went to other calls, including M8 sent 5.86 mi to chest pain IC-005, so the ALS shortage came from the agent's own allocation.
